label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Here's the reply, written as Hélène posting on the board:

---

**Re: Pétrin Doré on Fairmount closing?? sign in the window**

Hello everyone, and thank you D. Bergeron for asking straight. You are right that people deserve a straight answer, so here it is, today, well before the 4th.

**We are not closing. We are buying the building.**

First, one small thing: my name is Hélène, I'm the owner of Le Pétrin Doré. I think the name got mixed up with Mme Gagnon somewhere, but I wanted to introduce myself properly since I'm the one answering.

Now, the story, and it's actually a nice one.

The owner of the building at 5 rue Fairmount (corner) is M. Ferland. He is 81 years old and he is retiring to Sherbrooke to live near his daughter. He came to see me before he made any plans with anybody else — he came to see me, and he offered to sell it to me. We signed at the notary on December 15. It's done. It's mine now, and I am the baker who gets to keep paying the mortgage instead of paying rent to a landlord. I know what Marc-Antoine's cousin said is half right: yes, the building was sold in the fall. It was sold to me. There is no condo project, no bank, no vape shop. The three apartments upstairs stay apartments, and so does the bakery.

M. Ferland came to the bakery every single morning for 17 years. Every morning. For his baguette *pas trop cuite*, which I could never get right for anybody else, so he always waited for his. He cried a little bit at the notary. I cried a bit too. He's 81 and he was the first person to believe in this corner when I opened in March 2009. If anyone tells you I ran off with the money, please come and meet him, he can tell you himself.

**About the sign.** Yes, I know. "Fermé du 4 au 18 janvier. Grande nouvelle bientôt!" It wasn't very clear and I'm sorry about that. My nephew Thomas wrote it at 6 in the morning, and the "grande nouvelle" was his idea, not mine. I said "ok" without really thinking about it because I was happy and I didn't want to give it away. I was going to keep the surprise for the reopening. Some of you noticed it and started worrying, and I understand why, and I'm sorry I let the mystery grow for a couple of days. That's on me, not on the bakery.

**About the half empty shelves on the 28th.** We sold everything for Christmas Eve. 400 bûches. That's all it was. If you saw bare shelves that morning, it's because there was nothing left to put on them. We'll be fully stocked from the 19th, I promise.

**Now, the carnets, because this is the important part and I want to be very clear.**

- We sold **214 carnets** in October.
- They are **$60 for 12 loaves**.
- **Every single one of them is still valid. Every one. There is no expiry date.** No carnet expires, none of them, not one, ever.
- When we reopen, **every carnet holder gets 1 free croissant in January**, on top of their 12 loaves.
- And if anybody genuinely wants their money back, come and see me and I will give it to you, in full, the same day, no question, no argument, no form to fill out. I'd rather lose the money than have one person on this street think I took their $60 and ran.

D. Bergeron, you asked what happens to the carnets. The answer is: they get honoured, that's what happens to them. And if that answer isn't enough for you, then come in and talk to me in person, I'd really rather shake your hand than argue with you on a message board.

**About the two weeks.** We're closed **from January 4 to January 18** for the works. Yes, the sign says "Fermé", and yes, it's two weeks, and yes, "grande nouvelle" was an over-excuse, but here's what's actually happening in those two weeks:

- We're installing a **new deck oven, 4 decks**, coming from our supplier in Laval. The old oven is from **1998** and it broke three times this year. Three times. Each time we lost a morning of production. I was not going to open a bakery in 2026 with an oven from 1998.
- We're taking over the space at the back, which used to be the old dépanneur storage room. It's being redone and we're putting in **6 small tables**, so finally people can sit down and eat there instead of standing on the sidewalk like pigeons.

**We reopen on Tuesday, January 19, at 7:00 in the morning.** That's our regular time, that's when the first loaves come out, and the door is open.

**And I want to invite all of you to come on Saturday, January 23.** That's the day after, and it's for you. From 9 in the morning, **coffee and a piece of the new bread, free**, for everybody who shows up. Bring the kids, bring your neighbours, bring the people who said "oh she's closing" last week, I don't care, come get the coffee. If the oven behaves, there will be baguettes *pas trop cuite* at the back and I'll save one for M. Ferland if he comes to visit. I heard he might.

**One more thing, for the neighbours.** The **three apartments upstairs stay rented**, to the same tenants, at the same rent. I've promised that to them **in writing**, and I'll put it in writing again for anyone who wants to see it. Nobody upstairs is losing their home because I bought the building. If you're a tenant up there and you've read this thread, please come and talk to me, or call the bakery, and I'll show you the paper.

D. Bergeron, you wrote that people deserve a straight answer instead of a surprise. You're right, and thank you for pushing. You get one now, in full, four days before we even close: **not closing, buying the building, new oven, reopening the 19th at 7am, party on the 23rd, carnets honoured, no expiry, money back any time if you want it.** If there's anything else you're worried about, ask me here and I'll answer.

And thank you to **Priya S.**, who said the words I needed to hear before I could even post this. You gave my kid a free chocolatine every Saturday for a year and I never thanked you properly, so thank you now. Thank you to the other people who stood up for us, to the ones who came by to check the sign, and to the ones who simply asked first instead of assuming the worst. And to Marc-Antoine's cousin, who got half of it right — the sale was real, just not the ending you were expecting.

I know Mile End has lost a lot of small shops. I know people are tired of being surprised by closures, and I understand the worry. But a scam? After **17 years** on this street, that one hurt. I don't want a fight with anybody, not with you, not with noodle_and_crumb, not with anyone. I just want to bake bread and feed the neighbourhood, and I'd like to do it in a building that belongs to me so I never have to wonder about it again.

So: **January 19 at 7am, and Saturday January 23 for coffee and bread. Come see us. The oven is new, the shelves will be full, and we'll still be here.**

— **Hélène**, *Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré*, 5 rue Fairmount (corner)

reasons: facts: it says the building was sold "in the fall" although the notary signing was December 15, says "four days before we even close" when the post date of Dec 28 is six days before Jan 4, and calls Jan 23 "the day after" the Jan 19 reopening.
